answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate hardware-backed remote attestation. Identities execute within an enclave opaque as onyx, using burnt-in silicon keys to sign state proofs. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing scarce secure silicon per identity, facing a steep capital ledge. A protocol lantern audits these certificates before granting admission. However, this relies on centralized hardware vendors, and microarchitectural side channels can expose root keys.
